beats.text: One leg or two: which tires a flamingo?
beats.visual_intent: frame 0: two flamingos side by side, one leg vs two legs, question mark

beats.text: One leg looks like hard work.
beats.visual_intent: a person wobbling on one leg, sweating

beats.text: But in 2017, scientists propped up a dead flamingo.
beats.visual_intent: lab bench, flamingo with X eyes held upright by a clamp

beats.text: It settled onto one leg and stayed put, with no muscles working.
beats.visual_intent: the X-eyed flamingo locked on one leg, a padlock pops on the ankle

beats.text: On two legs, it wouldn't stay steady.
beats.visual_intent: same flamingo on two legs, tipping, motion lines, a cross

beats.text: Live flamingos even swayed less when they dozed off.
beats.visual_intent: sleeping flamingo on one leg, sway marks shrinking, zz

beats.text: They also do it more in water, and more as it gets colder, which may save heat.
beats.visual_intent: flamingo in cold water, thermometer low, heat kept in the body

beats.text: So one leg isn't hard work. It's how a flamingo rests.
beats.visual_intent: big REST POSE text beside a relaxed flamingo

beats.text: Two legs is the pose that needs muscle. Did you guess right?
beats.visual_intent: back to the two flamingos, the two-legged one sweating, question mark

title_options: Why flamingos stand on one leg (it's the easy pose)
A dead flamingo can still balance on one leg
publish.description: A 2017 experiment propped up a dead flamingo: it locked onto one leg with no muscle, but would not stay steady on two.

cta.decision_reason: the hook asks viewers to pick one leg or two; asking whether they guessed right turns that pick into a comment and closes the loop
